title: Sell Mineral Rights in Newburg, ND
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Newburg, ND
metaDescription: Inherited mineral rights near Newburg, Bottineau County, ND? Get a clear read on what a flank-area interest is worth before you sign anything.
heroLead: Newburg families who still hold mineral acreage usually got it the same way most Bottineau County owners did: a homestead passed down, a lease signed once, and then decades of silence.
intro: Newburg is small, close to the Souris River valley, and far enough from the Bakken core that most of the oil talk in this part of the state skips right past it. But Bottineau County has a real, if modest, oil history of its own, and some Newburg-area tracts carry old leases or small legacy production that's easy to overlook if you're not the one who signed the original paperwork.

sections.heading: A quieter oil history than the Bakken counties
paragraphs: The wells that have gone in around Bottineau County over the decades have mostly targeted shallower conventional zones rather than the deep Bakken shale that drives the boom-town headlines further west. Production here tends to be smaller and steadier rather than a sharp spike and decline, which changes how a buyer values the interest but doesn't erase its worth.

sections.heading: Sorting out what your family actually owns
paragraphs: It's common for Newburg-area mineral interests to have passed through two or three generations without a formal deed update, which means the name on file at the courthouse may not match who actually owns the interest today. We check the chain of title before we ever put a number in front of you, so there are no surprises partway through.

sections.heading: Why an honest look matters more here than the number itself
paragraphs: Because so little drilling has happened around Newburg in recent years compared to the Bakken core, it's easy for an owner to assume the interest is worthless and either ignore an offer or accept whatever number shows up first. We'd rather tell you plainly whether there's real value to work with than let either extreme happen.

faqs.question: Nobody in my family has ever collected a royalty on this interest. Is it still worth checking?
faqs.answer: Yes. A lot of Newburg-area minerals have never been drilled or leased recently, but that can change, and even undeveloped acreage sometimes has value. It's worth a quick title check before assuming there's nothing there.

faqs.question: How do I know which county office holds the records for my Newburg property?
faqs.answer: Newburg falls under Bottineau County. We pull records from the Bottineau County Recorder directly so you don't have to track them down yourself.

faqs.question: What paperwork do I need if I inherited this from a parent who passed years ago?
faqs.answer: Generally a probate record or affidavit of heirship showing the transfer of ownership, plus a notarized deed to complete a sale. We can tell you exactly what's needed once we see your specific situation.

faqs.question: Is it possible our family's interest was never actually recorded correctly?
faqs.answer: It happens more often than you'd expect with older Bottineau County paperwork. We check the recorder's file directly and flag any gaps before we make an offer.
